findings.title: SQL injection reachable from search endpoint
findings.why_vulnerable: Same unparameterized SQL build reached from the public search route.
findings.exploit_scenario: Anonymous attacker injects via q to read data.
findings.variants: Also reachable via the /api/v2/search alias; verify both routes.

findings.title: IDOR: order access without ownership check
findings.vulnerable_flow: GET /api/orders/<id> -> get_order() -> repo.find(id) with no owner check
findings.why_vulnerable: The order is fetched purely by client-supplied id; no check binds the order to the caller.
findings.exploit_scenario: An authenticated user iterates order ids to read other customers' orders.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant data disclosure of all orders.
findings.recommended_fix: Enforce an ownership/authorization check binding order.owner to the caller.
findings.action_plan: Add a policy check in get_order and a test for cross-user access denial.
findings.missing_tests: No test asserts a user cannot read another user's order.
findings.variants: Audit all repo.find(id) call sites in src/api for the same pattern.
findings.live_verification_plan: With authorization, request two order ids belonging to a test account only; no enumeration of real users, no automation.

findings.title: Service banner disclosure
findings.why_vulnerable: A version banner is exposed; informational at most.
findings.recommended_fix: Consider removing the version banner from responses.
